findings.evidence: `sizeImpactParameterEquiv`'s `map_add'`/`map_smul'` (257-258) are discharged by `simp`, i.e. only `size_add`/`impactParameter_add`/`size_smul`/`impactParameter_smul` are load-bearing; the zero/neg/sub lemmas are consequences of those two, not independent facts.
findings.fix: Move the bundled map ahead of these lemmas — build `sizeImpactParameterEquiv` (or a pair of `Dipole →ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` maps) from `size_add`/`size_smul`/`impactParameter_add`/`impactParameter_smul` alone, then derive the other six from `map_zero`, `map_neg`, `map_sub` (e.g. `size_sub d d' := congrArg Prod.fst (sizeImpactParameterEquiv.map_sub d d')`).
findings.issue: `size_zero` (167), `impactParameter_zero` (169), `size_neg` (181), `impactParameter_neg` (185), `size_sub` (189) and `impactParameter_sub` (193) are special cases of the linearity that `sizeImpactParameterEquiv` (253) establishes, but each gets its own bespoke proof via a different route (`abel`, `module`, `midpoint_vsub_midpoint`, `simp [impactParameter_def]`). Four distinct Mathlib midpoint/algebra lemmas are invoked to prove four instances of the same linear-map property.

findings.evidence: `rapidity_le_rapidity_iff_ge` (107-109) gives `rapidity x₀ x ≤ rapidity x₀ x' ↔ x' ≤ x`; instantiating `x := 1`, `x' := x` yields `rapidity x₀ 1 ≤ rapidity x₀ x ↔ x ≤ 1`, and `rapidity x₀ 1 = Real.log (x₀ / 1) = Real.log x₀`.
findings.fix: Keep the `x₀ = 0` case split, and in the `x₀ ≠ 0` branch use `(rapidity_le_rapidity_iff_ge hx₀ one_pos hx).2 hx1` rewritten with `rapidity_def, div_one` instead of repeating `rapidity_eq_log_sub_log` + `Real.log_nonpos`.
findings.issue: Same pattern: `log_le_rapidity` re-derives the log algebra by hand, but for `x₀ ≠ 0` it is exactly the antitonicity lemma proved 10 lines above, since `rapidity x₀ 1 = Real.log x₀`.

summary: Assumptions in both files are minimal and the abstraction level matches the roadmap target. The one generality defect is in Coordinates.lean: linearity of `size` and `impactParameter` is reproved six times as separate special cases (zero, neg, sub) instead of being derived from the linear isomorphism the file already constructs.
